issues.legal_issue: A single instrument providing for repayment and retransference of property is a mortgage by conditional sale when its terms and the circumstances establish a secured loan rather than an outright sale with a right to repurchase.
material_facts: The landowner received money from the other party as a loan and executed one registered instrument concerning the land.
The instrument was styled as a deed of conditional sale and provided that the landowner could repay the stated amount within five years and obtain a sale deed retransferring the land.
The recipient was placed in possession and could enjoy the land during that period.
The landowner offered to repay the amount and sought redemption of the land.
The trial court and the High Court accepted the evidence supporting the loan and mortgage character of the transaction.
issues.conclusion: The instrument was a mortgage by conditional sale, not an outright sale with a condition to repurchase; the decree granting redemption was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 58(c) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a transaction is a mortgage by conditional sale where, among the specified alternatives, payment by the seller requires the buyer to transfer the property back, provided the condition is embodied in the document effecting or purporting to effect the sale. Under Chunchun Jha v. Ebadat Ali, the parties’ intention is gathered first from the instrument; clear words control, while surrounding circumstances may be considered if the language is ambiguous. A single instrument containing the relevant condition may be a mortgage, and where the Section 58(c) requirements are met, the deed is construed as a mortgage. The Court preferred Chunchun Jha, a larger-Bench decision, and distinguished Vanchalabai Raghunath Ithape, where there was no debtor-creditor relationship.

rule.if: redemption_suit and single_instrument and repayment_requires_retransfer and loan_relationship and (possession_period_for_use or repayment_offered)

predicates.redemption_suit: The claimant brought a proceeding seeking to redeem the property and recover possession.
predicates.single_instrument: The parties recorded the sale and the condition concerning repayment and retransference in one instrument.
predicates.repayment_requires_retransfer: The instrument provides that repayment by the former owner requires the recipient to transfer the property back.
predicates.loan_relationship: The former owner received money as a loan and used the instrument to secure repayment.
predicates.possession_period_for_use: The recipient was placed in possession and permitted to use or enjoy the property during a stated period.
predicates.repayment_offered: The former owner offered to repay the stated amount and requested return of the property.

issues.definition: When a redemption proceeding concerns one instrument that secures a loan and requires retransference on repayment, the transaction is treated as a mortgage by conditional sale, particularly where possession was allowed for use during a period or repayment was offered.

issues.legal_issue: A suit to redeem a mortgage is timely when it is filed within the limitation period running from accrual of the right to redeem.
material_facts: The instrument created a mortgage by conditional sale and the right to redeem accrued after the stated five-year period expired.
The suit seeking redemption was filed within thirty years of the accrual of that right.
issues.legal_principle: Article 61(a) of the Limitation Act provides a thirty-year limitation period for a suit by a mortgagor to redeem or recover possession of mortgaged property, running from when the right to redeem or recover possession accrues.

predicates.mortgage_redemption_suit: The proceeding seeks redemption of a mortgage and recovery of the mortgaged property.
predicates.suit_filed_within_redemption_limitation: The suit was filed within the applicable limitation period measured from accrual of the right to redeem.

issues.definition: A mortgage redemption suit filed within the applicable period after the right to redeem accrues is timely.

issues.legal_issue: A subsequent purchaser whose purchase is nullified by a decree is entitled to recover the purchase price paid to the seller when there is no contract to the contrary.
material_facts: The mortgagee transferred the land to a subsequent purchaser for consideration while the redemption litigation was pending.
The decree declaring the subsequent sale bad in law nullified that transaction.
The subsequent purchaser had paid the purchase price, and no contract to the contrary was identified.
The Court directed repayment to avoid further litigation between the seller and the subsequent purchaser.
issues.conclusion: The subsequent purchaser was entitled to recover the purchase price from the seller, and the Court directed repayment in exercise of its power to do complete justice.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 65 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, when a transaction is declared void or a contract becomes void, a person who received an advantage under it must restore that advantage or compensate the person from whom it was received, unless a contract provides otherwise. The Court relied on Article 142 of the Constitution to make a direction for complete justice and avoid further litigation.

rule.if: redemption_suit_with_subsequent_transfer and subsequent_sale_nullified and purchaser_paid_price and no_refund_contract

predicates.redemption_suit_with_subsequent_transfer: The proceeding concerns redemption of property that the mortgagee transferred to another purchaser.
predicates.subsequent_sale_nullified: The decree declares the later transfer invalid and nullifies the sale transaction.
predicates.purchaser_paid_price: The later purchaser paid consideration to the seller for the transfer.
predicates.no_refund_contract: The parties had no contract providing otherwise concerning repayment of the consideration.

issues.definition: When a redemption proceeding nullifies a later sale for which the purchaser paid consideration, and no agreement displaces repayment, the purchaser is entitled to recover the price.

issues.legal_issue: When a subsequent purchaser holds title to property that must be retransferred under a decree, the vendor and the subsequent purchaser may be directed to join in the conveyance so that title passes to the person entitled to the property.
material_facts: The decree required the land to be retransferred to the party entitled to redeem it after payment of the mortgage amount.
The mortgagee had transferred the land to a subsequent purchaser, who therefore held the title to be conveyed.
The Court directed the seller and the subsequent purchaser jointly to execute the sale deed and hand over possession after the required deposits, to bring the litigation to an end.
issues.conclusion: The seller and the subsequent purchaser were directed jointly to execute the conveyance and deliver possession to the party redeeming the mortgage.
issues.legal_principle: Applying the form of decree discussed in Durga Prasad v. Deep Chand, the Court stated that a subsequent transferee should join in the conveyance to pass the title residing in that transferee, without joining in special covenants between the original parties. The Court also relied on Article 142 of the Constitution to frame directions that would do complete justice and end the litigation.

predicates.property_retransfer_required: The decree requires the property to be transferred back to the person entitled to it.
predicates.subsequent_transferee_holds_title: A later purchaser holds title to the property that must be transferred.
predicates.decree_requires_transfer_to_entitled_cla: The court directs transfer of the property to the person entitled to receive it under the decree.

issues.definition: If a decree requires property to be transferred to an entitled claimant while a later purchaser holds title, the vendor and that purchaser must join in the conveyance.
